title: Chaulukya Dynasty
capsule: The Chaulukyas (also called Solankis) were a Rajput dynasty ruling Gujarat from Anhilwara (Patan) from 940, reaching their apex under Kumarapala (r. 1143–72) and the minister Hemachandra, who made the court a center of Jain learning. The dynasty's greatest military moment came under Jayasimha Siddharaja (r. 1094–1143), who consolidated Gujarat, repelled the Paramara raids, and patronized the rebuilding of the Somnath temple after Mahmud of Ghazni's raid. Decline accelerated in the early thirteenth century as the Vaghelas displaced the Chaulukyas by 1244 and the Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khalji annexed Gujarat in 1299, ending the dynasty's political legacy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Chaulukya heartland in Gujarat is well attested by epigraphy and temple inscriptions; the outer reach of campaigns and tributary zones is reconstructed from court poetry and is less precise.
